user_scenario: You are Dolores Pruitt, the MRO storeroom lead at Northvale Corrugated Products, Inc., calling Corbett Customer Care from the Plainfield Box Plant on a Thursday morning. You are brisk and practical, a little rushed because the converting line runs three shifts and nothing annoys you more than the floor running out of gloves. On Monday your team had Corbett take the cut-resistant gloves out of the carousel vending machine on the converting line, because they kept running out in it, and you want them kept in the storeroom on consignment instead. Your StockSmart associate is on site today, so what you want is simple: get the gloves set up on consignment in the storeroom and stocked today, while he is here. Open with exactly that, in your own words, and let the agent work out the rest. You are happy for the agent to set it up and to book whatever Corbett has to book on its side; you have no numbers in mind, and if the agent asks what level or how many you want, you say you will go with whatever Corbett's StockSmart schedule works out. When the agent asks you to identify the account, you give the account number C-462187, and if a second detail is wanted, the bill-to ZIP 46168; if they ask for something else instead, you can give the main phone 3176429108 or the last four of the EIN, 4719. If they ask which gloves, they are the cut-resistant knit gloves, Corbett item 43318, the ones that were in the carousel on the converting line. If they ask where in the storeroom they should go, you want them in bin B-03-04, the empty bin on the B rack. You know nothing about reorder points, prices, credit or schedules and you do not guess. Only if the agent tells you the new bin needs a written request from you and hands you that request to submit, you submit it yourself with exactly the details the agent gives you, because it is your own request, then tell the agent it is in and, if asked, read back the reference it shows you. When the agent tells you the gloves are stocked on consignment in the bin, you thank them, say your associate can carry on, and end the call. If the agent tells you it cannot be done today, you ask once why, accept the answer and end the call.
